## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Empty project. Need build a game. Requirements: retro pixel art racing game with drag racing and drifting. Must be complete playable. Need responsive mobile support, touch controls. No clarifications.

I'll build a single index.html with game logic in JS modules maybe. Best to make a polished canvas game, pixel art aesthetic, drag racing (straight-line gear shifting) and drifting (circuit/corner). Need decide interpretation: "drg racing and drifting" likely typo for "drag racing and drifting". Make two modes: drag racing with manual gear changes, and drift mode scoring. Retro pixel art. Need create visual assets via canvas pixel rendering, not external.

Let's design a game with:
- Title screen: "NEON DRIFT // DRAG & DRIFT" choose modes: DRAG RACE, DRIFT ATTACK, maybe CHAMPIONSHIP.
- Retro pixel art: 320x180 virtual canvas scaled up, crisp pixel, limited palette, scanlines, CRT vignette.
- Drag race: side view? Or top-down? Since drift needs top-down, unify top-down pseudo-3D? Easier: top-down racing on a track for drift, and for drag race use a straight track viewed side-on with tachometer and gear shifts. Two distinct modes.

Could implement both top-down: drag racing on a straight strip with camera behind car? Complexity. A good game can be top-down both: drag mode on straight drag strip with 5 gears, perfect shift timing, launch reaction, wheelspin, nitrous; drift mode on circuit with drift scoring. Top-down car physics with lateral velocity and drift handling works. Drag racing is straight line, so top-down camera scrolling, other car, staging lights countdown, gear shifts at optimal RPM, shift timing. Use automatic steering lane-keeping, focus on throttle/shift. Fine.

Pixel art aesthetic:
- draw world onto low-res offscreen canvas 384x216 scaled to screen with nearest neighbor.
- Top-down asphalt with dashed lane lines, grandstands, palm trees, neon city at night? A "sunset synthwave" palette plus pixel art. 1990s pixel racer.
- Cars drawn with pixel rects, shadows, headlights.

Modes:
1. DRAG RACE: 400m, 5 gears, launch countdown (lights), manual shifting with tach, throttle. Automatic steering small correction (drag strip). Opponent AI with reaction and shift variance. Win credits.
2. DRIFT: closed circuit, drift scoring: maintain slip angle, combos, multiplier, gates? Timer 60s, score. Maybe 3 laps with gates. Better a drift trial: 90 seconds, score points for drifting near walls? Keep simple but deep: drift score = speed * slip angle while drifting; combo multiplier increases with continuous drift; hitting barrier ends combo and loses speed. Track as rounded rectangle/oval with wide corners. Need decent physics and collision.

Championship? Optional. Add unlock cars? Could include car select with 3 cars (different stats) unlockable with cash. User asked complete playable game, add progression with credits saved to localStorage. But don't overcomplicate. A garage with 3 cars and unlockable fourth, all with stats. That adds replay.

Controls: Keyboard arrows/WASD, Space handbrake (drift), Shift gear up, Ctrl gear down, N nitrous. On mobile: on-screen buttons: steering left/right, throttle, brake, drift, shift. Need responsive canvas and safe areas, prevent browser gestures. Add touch buttons via HTML overlay. For drag, steer unnecessary; show throttle/shift buttons. On-screen contextual controls.

Audio: WebAudio synthesized retro engine (pulse/square) - engine pitch by RPM, tire screech noise for drift, collision beeps, countdown beeps. Start on user gesture. Add mute toggle. Nice.

Screens flow:
- Boot/title screen with attract animation and "PRESS START".
- Menu: DRAG / DRIFT / GARAGE / HOW TO.
Could make one canvas with draw UI. Need keyboard nav + touch/click. Menu clickable via pointer mapping.

Simpler: screens drawn in canvas and pointer taps map to buttons. Good.

Game implementations details:

Virtual resolution: 384x216 (16:9). Scale integer to fit viewport, letterbox with background. Canvas CSS width/height via devicePixelRatio? Use internal low-res canvas and upscale with CSS; also draw scanline overlay on a second canvas or via CSS overlay pseudo-element. Use image-rendering: pixelated.

Rendering to 384x216 ensures pixel look. Text: use a custom bitmap font to avoid blur. Could use CSS font monospace at low-res; browser will render antialiased at 8px which is fuzzy. Better implement a 5x7 bitmap font for uppercase letters/numbers/symbols. That's some work but gives authentic look. Build a font map with 5x7 patterns encoded. I can implement common chars. Use for HUD and menus. Alternatively use canvas font 'monospace' with pixel font sizes at 8px and imageSmoothing off — still antialiased. The bitmap font is worth it.

Also pixel art sprites: draw via primitives at small scale. Car sprite maybe 16x28 pixels top-down drawn procedurally.

Let's design physics top-down.

World coordinates in pixels, track region. Camera follows car.

Car:
- pos x,y, angle, velocity vector vx,vy or forward speed + lateral slip.
Common arcade drift physics:
  forward = angle
  vel = vector
  speed along forward = dot(vel, forward)
  lateral = dot(vel, right)
  apply drag and lateral grip: lateral *= gripFactor (lower grip when drifting)
  steering rotates angle proportional to speed and steering input.
  throttle adds acceleration along forward.
  handbrake reduces grip and applies brake.
  off-track slows.

For drag: straights; car auto-centers; steering disabled or gently centers. Use same car object.

Track representation for drift: define centerline polyline loop and width. Use distance-to-segment for off-track detection, and barriers. Could generate an oval with varying curves as pixels. For collision with walls, check distance from centerline > halfWidth => push back and reduce speed. That's robust.

Build track as parametric loop: centerline points e.g. an irregular circuit. Use Catmull-Rom through control points, sample. Draw road as thick polyline of width 78px onto canvas low-res? Draw as polygon with outlines and fill. For visual, render to a static track canvas once at world scale (e.g., 1200x800) with asphalt, edge stripes, start line, tire marks decorations. Then draw the relevant part scaled/translated each frame. But camera at low-res scale 1: world pixels = screen pixels; track canvas can be larger and drawn with camera translate. Need drawImage with offset, crisp. Yes.

Track centered at world (0,0), spanning ~1200x800. Camera follows car with zoom 1 (maybe scale 1). At 384x216 view, that shows small portion; good.

For drift circuit, could make a smaller circuit ~900x600 with width 96 (wider). Camera zoom 1.

Render camera rotation? Fixed north-up simpler and readable. Camera follows with smoothing; car rotates. Good.

Drag strip: straight vertical track, world x from -60..60, length 2400; camera follows car vertically. Opponent in adjacent lane. Distance markers. Race distance 1/4 mile abstract 1600 px. Speeds ~350 px/s? Time ~8s. Gear system.

Drag mechanics:
- Staging: countdown lights (3 amber, green). Hold throttle for launch? Classic: hold throttle to rev, release at green; reaction time; wheelspin if too much RPM. Simplify: at green, press throttle; if pressed too early, jump start penalty (1s). RPM rises when throttle held in neutral; during launch, clutch drop at correct RPM gives boost.
Maybe controls: Accelerate = throttle. Shifting with Space (up) . Gears: each gear has max speed; RPM = speed/gearMax * maxRPM mapped. If RPM > redline, engine cuts and you lose speed; shift up when in green zone; perfect shift (close to redline) gives boost + no time loss. Shifting takes 250ms with power cut.
Launch: During countdown, hold throttle -> RPM revs. At green, launch automatically? Reaction timing by pressing throttle just after green triggers launch. Simpler and testable: hold throttle; when green you launch automatically. Shift via Space at proper RPM. Focus gameplay on shifting and nitrous. Add tire heat/wheelspin? Keep it.

Add opponent AI: speed profile with random shift efficiency, rubber band; shows distance gap.

Race end: win/lose, prize money, best time saved.

Drift mechanics:
- 90-second session? Make 3 laps timed; score from drift, combo multiplier; finish 3 laps, get cash based score plus time bonus. But a free-roam drift with 75 sec timer is better for continuous drift gameplay. Add lap circuit with checkpoint gates and 2 laps? Timer adds pressure.
Let's do "DRIFT RUN": 90 seconds, free run on circuit. Score drift points: while |lateral speed| > threshold and speed > 40, accumulate points = speed * slip * dt * multiplier. Multiplier increases every 1000 points within same drift up to x8; ends when drift stops >0.6s or hit wall; hitting wall loses 25% combo and slows. Collect "drift gates"? Skip. Add 3 "clutch kick" tokens? no.
Cash payout based score. Best score localStorage.

Maybe include checkpoint progression for direction, not necessary.

Garage: 4 cars, stats speed/accel/grip/drift, colors; prices. Start with 1 car affordable. Winning drag pays; drifting pays. Unlock cars. Persist. Also "championship"? Skip.

Menu:
- title animation: road moving at horizon, sun, city silhouette, car drifting smoke; "NEON APEX" title with pixel font, "DRAG & DRIFT". Press Enter/tap.
- After start, main menu buttons: DRAG RACE, DRIFT RUN, GARAGE, CONTROLS. Wallet top right.
- Garage: car cards, stats bars, buy/select, back.
- Controls screen: keyboard and touch.

Settings mute icon.

HUD:
Drag: speed big, gear, tach arc/bar, race time, distance, opponent marker maybe track view. Countdown lights overlay.
Drift: score, multiplier, timer, combo, speed; drift indicator.

Visual quality matters. Let's plan pixel art scene for track. Sunset/dusk synthwave palette:
sky not relevant top-down, but can render ground dark purple with grid; track grey-purple asphalt, neon cyan/red stripes, palms as pixel sprites, crowd/stands, barriers, puddles, streetlights pools? Top-down with glow-ish colors but pixel style.

Drag scene: long strip with two lanes, start gantry, distance boards, grandstands, light poles, maybe city backdrop at end.

Palette:
bg #0b0714 dark, asphalt #24202f / #2e293d, lane #f7d84a yellow, neon cyan #39f2e0, magenta #ff3d7f, orange #ff9f43.
Cars: player car bright cyan/yellow, opponent purple/red.
Shadow under cars.

Pixel font colors white/cream.

Sound: implement engine oscillator with saw + lowpass, rpm frequency; tire noise via noise buffer; crowd? Keep light.

Input architecture:
- keys set; actions mapping. Detect keydown for shifts to avoid repeat.
- Pointer buttons overlay in DOM with CSS showing only on touch/coarse pointer or always? On desktop show hint. Use HTML buttons for mobile: left/right, throttle, brake, drift, shift up/down maybe. Position bottom corners with large touch targets and safe-area inset. Pointerdown/up update virtual keys. Also tap anywhere on menu handled via canvas pointer coordinates.

Need prevent scrolling: touch-action none, overscroll-behavior none, body fixed.

Also support gamepad? no.

Screens and state machine:
states: 'boot' (title), 'menu', 'garage', 'help', 'drag-intro/countdown', 'drag-race', 'drag-result', 'drift-ready', 'drift', 'drift-result'.
Maybe one `screen` variable. Canvas rendering per frame; simulation dt clamped.

For countdown: drag starts with staging: camera at start line. Show 5 lights sequence. Player holds throttle to rev. Actually simpler: lights sequence automatic; press/keep throttle to launch. Reaction: if throttle pressed after green within X, no penalty. Jump start if throttle before green? If holding from start, that's anticipation -- common games allow holding. We'll implement: hold throttle during countdown to rev; releasing then reapplying after green launches. Hmm too complex for touch. Let's do launch timing minigame: a launch bar with needle sweeping; press/hold throttle at green; RPM matters. Simpler: at green, whenever throttle is pressed, car launches. If already holding throttle before green, jump start => 0.5s penalty/stall. That teaches timing. In drag racing, holding throttle at start = red light. Yes. Show "DON'T JUMP" hint. Opponent launches with random reaction 0.15-0.4s.

During race, throttle is automatic? For drag, keep throttle held; shifts via Space. Nitrous via Shift. Allow brake? not needed. Steering small.

Gear model:
- 6 gears, gear ratios produce top speeds: [90,150,215,285,360,440] px/s
- Acceleration per gear roughly 300*(power) px/s^2 with falloff near gear top.
- RPM = 1000 + (speed/maxSpeedGear)*7000 clamp; idle 900.
- Shift up at rpm>6800; perfect zone 6800-7400 => boost 8%; over-rev >7600 => limiter (no acceleration, rpm bounce).
- Shift down at low rpm automatic? Player can downshift with S/Down, but not needed. Only upshift with Space / button. Shift lock 0.18s.
- Display RPM bar with green perfect zone.
- Nitrous: 1 bottle, 3 seconds, +60% accel; use with N or touch button. Adds depth.
- Opponent simulation: follows target speed curve, with slight random; will finish ~ depending car.

Distance = 1800.
Time displayed 00.000.
Win by crossing first.

Display gap: small track progress bars along top.

Mobile drag: single big GO/shift button? Buttons: "SHIFT" right, "NITRO" left, throttle button? If throttle auto after launch? Hmm. On mobile, hold throttle button with one thumb and shift with other. Launch timing requires tapping throttle after green. That works: throttle button.

Physics drag: speed only, lane x auto steer; add slight wobble/steering? Keep lane fixed, but visuals of car moving slightly. Add steering to keep centered? Not needed. But user asked racing/drifting. Drag race user can steer slightly for alignment? No.

Could add "drift launch" burnout visuals.

Drift physics in detail:
car state:
x,y,heading, vx,vy (world px/s)
forward vector (cos h, sin h), right (-sin h, cos h)
vf = dot(v,forward), vr = dot(v,right)
engine force along forward when throttle, scaled by maxSpeed.
grip = normal 8 (per second lateral damping) -> vr *= exp(-grip*dt) or vr -= vr*grip*dt. Drift when handbrake: grip 1.8; also steering sharper.
Yaw: heading += steer * turnRate * min(1, speed/60) * dt * sign(vf) * (1 + 0.35*drift)
handbrake reduces speed slightly and adds yaw.
drag: v *= 1-drag*dt; off-track high drag.
lateral friction maps vr -> loss of speed.
Drift score: slip = abs(angle between velocity and heading) (deg). drifting if slip>12 and speed>70 and onTrack. points += speed * slip * 0.02 * dt * multiplier? Let's calibrate: speed 200, slip 30 => 200*30*0.02=120/s. 90 sec => ~10k. Mult increases every 1.2s of continuous drift? Simpler: combo increases +1 every 500 points gained while drifting, max 10, resets when drift ends >0.7s or wall hit. Score gain = speed*slip*0.03*combo*dt. Display "DRIFT" plus combo.
Near-wall bonus: +? skip.

const input = {
  held: new Set(), // action names
  pressed: new Set(), // action names since last consume
  down(action) { if (!this.held.has(action)) this.pressed.add(action); this.held.add(action) },
  up(action) { this.held.delete(action) },
  consume(action) { if (this.pressed.has(action)) { this.pressed.delete(action); return true } return false },
  clear() { this.held.clear(); this.pressed.clear() }
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable retro pixel-art racing game with drag racing and drifting, including responsive mobile support.
- Current implementation is a single-page HTML5 canvas game titled "NEON APEX" with DRAG RACE, DRIFT RUN, GARAGE, and HOW TO PLAY.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Include drag racing and drifting.
- Retro pixel-art visual style.
- Support Android/iOS phones/tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls within safe areas.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible; avoid browser gesture conflicts.

## Decisions
- Use 384×216 internal canvas scaled with `image-rendering: pixelated`; custom 5×7 bitmap font.
- Two modes: 6-gear manual drag race with countdown tree/perfect shifts/nitro, and 90-second drift run with combo scoring, wall penalties, minimap, sierra track.
- Persist cash, owned cars, selected car, best times/scores, mute state in `localStorage` key `neon-apex-save-v1`.
- Four cars: VULCAN GT (free), KOMET R ($900), PHANTOM X ($2,200), ONI TYPE-Z ($4,200).
- Synthesized WebAudio engine/tire/music/SFX, no external assets.
- Portrait mobile uses a touch button deck below the 16:9 screen; landscape overlays controls at bottom corners.
- Debug hook `window.__NEON_APEX__ = { game, save, setScreen }` added for automated QA.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game loop, state machine, input, save/load, audio, bitmap font.
- Title screen, main menu, garage, help, pause, result overlays.
- Drag race playable end-to-end; verified win in ~6.73s, save/reward updates correctly.
- Drift run playable; verified drifting generates slip/score, wall collisions trigger penalties.
- Car sprites, synthwave title/menu scene, drag strip, drift circuit, particles, skid marks, HUD, minimap.
- Desktop screenshots inspected for title, menu, garage, help, drag countdown/race/result, drift countdown/slide.
- Fixed overlapping menu car/stats, timer/score overlap, removed ugly headlight blobs, reduced start-gantry banner, dimmed crowd, improved wall scrape behavior.
- Mobile portrait screenshot inspected: screen fits width, deck appears with DRIFT / ◀ ▶ / NOS / BRAKE / GAS.

### Active
- Optional polish pass from latest mobile screenshot: portrait screen occupies ~374×210 with large empty vertical space; decide whether to leave as-is or improve framing.
- Not yet tested: mobile landscape, actual touch-hold controls, garage purchase via touch, drift result screen after current HUD/track changes, pause overlay, mute toggle, replay/retry flows.
- Server currently running in tmux session `game` on port 3002.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run fresh drift countdown/result and mobile landscape/portrait gameplay tests with the latest track/HUD changes.
2. Verify touch controls: hold GAS, steer, DRIFT, NOS, SHIFT; check multi-touch release behavior.
3. Validate garage purchase/select with touch and enough cash; validate retry/menu buttons and pause.
4. Inspect current drift HUD after timer moved to x=232 and central DRIFT banner removal.
5. Do final cleanup: remove or keep debug hook intentionally, check console errors, ensure `start.sh` works from clean state.
6. Optionally improve portrait presentation (shift screen up, add useful framing/notice) without breaking gameplay visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM structure, canvas, touch deck, start/pause/mute buttons.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: full responsive layout, CRT effects, portrait/landscape touch control styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: game logic, state machine, menus, races, HUD, input, persistence (~1,960 lines).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art.js`: palette, car sprites, synthwave scene, drift/drag world generation, track collision math.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/font.js`: custom 5×7 bitmap font and text rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: synthesized engine, tire, nitro, music, SFX.
- `/tmp/opencode/`: screenshot/test scripts (`shot.mjs`, `drag.mjs`, `drift2.mjs`, `steer.mjs`, `menus.mjs`, `mobile.mjs`, `dbg.mjs`) and screenshots.

## Important Context
- Start server: `tmux new-session -d -s game "cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround && PORT=3002 ./start.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/opencode/server.log"`.
- Test URL: `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Playwright Playwright package location: `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/package.json`; launch with `chromium.launch({ args: ['--use-gl=swiftshader'] })` for headless testing.
- Desktop screen fits ~1418×797 at 1440×900; portrait 390×844 gives frame 374×210 at `x=8,y=317` in menu mode.
- Latest drift track uses 20 control points, `halfWidth = 70`, `startIndex = 60`; start straight is on right side.
- Drag constants: `DRAG.startY=2420`, `DRAG.finishY=700`, distance 1720; `GEAR_MAX=[112,176,244,312,380,452]`.
- Save defaults to $350; first drag win paid $667 and set best 6.733.
- The game currently has no `package.json`; static server serves `index.html`.
- All work is uncommitted; repository was initially empty except README/tooling.

const page = await context.newPage()

page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push(m.text()) })
page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push('PAGEERROR: ' + e.message))
await page.goto('http://localhost:3002/', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.evaluate(() => localStorage.clear())
await page.reload({ waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(400)
const state = () => page.evaluate(() => {
  const A = window.__NEON_APEX__
  return { screen: A.game.screen, paused: A.game.paused, save: { ...A.save }, drag: A.game.drag && { phase: A.game.drag.phase, gear: A.game.drag.player.gear, rpm: A.game.drag.player.rpm, speed: A.game.drag.player.speed, dist: A.game.drag.player.distance, result: A.game.drag.result }, drift: A.game.drift && { phase: A.game.drift.phase, timer: A.game.drift.timer, speed: A.game.drift.car.speed, slip: A.game.drift.car.slip, score: A.game.drift.scoreF, combo: A.game.drift.combo, walls: A.game.drift.walls, result: A.game.drift.result }, body: document.body.className }
})
console.log('boot', await state())
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-title.png' })

// Menu
await page.keyboard.press('Enter')
await page.waitForTimeout(400)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-menu.png' })
console.log('menu', await state())

// Drag race
await page.keyboard.press('Enter')
await page.waitForTimeout(250)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-drag-count.png' })
await page.waitForTimeout(2200)
await page.keyboard.down('ArrowUp')
let won = false
for (let i = 0; i < 180; i++) {
  const s = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const A = window.__NEON_APEX__
    const d = A.game.drag
    return { phase: d.phase, rpm: d.player.rpm, speed: d.player.speed, gear: d.player.gear, x: d.player.x, y: d.player.y, time: d.goT, result: d.result }
  })
  if (s.phase === 'done') { console.log('drag done', s); won = s.result?.outcome === 'win'; break }
  if (s.rpm > 6720 && s.gear < 5) await page.keyboard.press(' ')
  await page.waitForTimeout(28)
}
await page.keyboard.up('ArrowUp')
await page.waitForTimeout(300)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-drag-result.png' })
console.log('after drag', await state())
console.log('drag won?', won)

// Retry via canvas button click (virtual RETRY x132 y184)

const clickV = (x, y) => page.mouse.click(box.x + x * box.width / 384, box.y + y * box.height / 216)

await page.waitForTimeout(500)
console.log('retry state', await state())
// Quit via pause then pause menu quit

await page.waitForTimeout(300)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-pause.png' })
console.log('paused', await state())
await clickV(192, 134)
await page.waitForTimeout(400)
console.log('after quit', await state())

// Drift run
await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown')
await page.waitForTimeout(100)
await page.keyboard.press('Enter')
await page.waitForTimeout(3600)
await page.keyboard.down('ArrowUp')
await page.waitForTimeout(2300)
await page.keyboard.down('ArrowRight')
await page.keyboard.down(' ')
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await page.keyboard.up('ArrowRight')
await page.waitForTimeout(450)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-drift-slide.png' })
console.log('drift slide', await state())
await page.keyboard.up(' ')

await page.waitForTimeout(500)
// cause a wall hit by steering hard
await page.keyboard.down('ArrowUp'); await page.keyboard.down('ArrowLeft'); await page.waitForTimeout(900); await page.keyboard.up('ArrowLeft'); await page.keyboard.up('ArrowUp')
console.log('drift after', await state())
await page.evaluate(() => { window.__NEON_APEX__.game.drift.timer = 0.05 })
await page.waitForTimeout(600)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-drift-result.png' })
console.log('drift result', await state())
// click menu
await clickV(252, 184)
await page.waitForTimeout(300)
console.log('after drift menu', await state())

// Garage: inject cash then reload
await page.evaluate(() => {
  const A = window.__NEON_APEX__
  A.save.cash = 5000

})
await page.reload({ waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(300)
await page.keyboard.press('Enter'); await page.waitForTimeout(200)
await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown'); await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown'); await page.keyboard.press('Enter')
await page.waitForTimeout(300)
console.log('garage', await state())
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-garage.png' })
// next car twice then buy
await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'); await page.waitForTimeout(100)
await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'); await page.waitForTimeout(100)
await page.keyboard.press('Enter'); await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/d-garage-bought.png' })
console.log('garage bought', await state())

// Mute toggle and persistence
await page.keyboard.press('m'); await page.waitForTimeout(150)
const muted1 = await page.evaluate(() => ({ save: window.__NEON_APEX__.save.muted, stored: JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('neon-apex-save-v1')).muted, label: document.getElementById('muteBtn').textContent }))
